name: Percona XtraDB Cluster
tagline: Percona Server plus Galera synchronous replication, packaged as an open-source HA MySQL cluster.
description: Percona XtraDB Cluster (PXC) combines Percona Server for MySQL with the Galera write-set replication library to give a virtually synchronous, multi-primary MySQL cluster. Every node holds a full copy of the data and commits are certified cluster-wide, so a node can fail without losing committed transactions. PXC adds Percona-specific safety rails such as strict mode, encrypted cluster traffic by default and ProxySQL integration, and it has a mature Kubernetes operator. It is a high-availability solution, not a write-scaling one: all nodes still apply every write.

pricing.notes: Free; Percona sells support and managed services.

scale.notes: Typically 3-5 nodes; writes are replicated to all nodes so throughput does not grow with node count. WAN clusters work but add commit latency.

strengths: No committed-data loss on single node failure thanks to certification-based synchronous replication
Any node accepts writes, simplifying failover
Automatic node provisioning via SST/IST with XtraBackup
Strict mode blocks unsafe operations (non-InnoDB tables, LOCK TABLES)
Percona Operator for MySQL (PXC) is production-proven on Kubernetes
weaknesses: Write throughput limited by the slowest node and network round trips
Optimistic certification causes deadlock errors on hot rows written from multiple nodes
Large transactions and DDL (TOI) stall the whole cluster
Needs at least three nodes (or an arbitrator) to avoid split brain
useCases: Highly available MySQL for business-critical OLTP
Zero-data-loss failover within a data center
Self-hosted MySQL on Kubernetes with an operator
Read scaling with consistent reads on every node
notIdealFor: Write-heavy workloads that need horizontal write scaling
Very large single transactions or bulk loads
